reproduced: official SPARC Table 1 contains 175 rows with Q counts 99/64/12
Q in {1,2} and inclination >= 30 degrees selects 153 objects, matching the SPARC master paper's final science sample
all 153 selected names have entries in the staged 175-profile Rotmod_LTG.zip
SPARC .dens decomposition entries contain radial surface luminosity densities, not 3D density maps
literature_read: SPARC master paper's stellar and gas geometry prescriptions, HI-profile availability caveat, and quality-selection rule
TG NGC 3198 solver boundary conditions and spherical component-velocity-to-density construction as printed in the supplied paper

sample.selection_rule: Q in {1,2}; inclination >= 30 deg; no Vflat cut

split.algorithm: Sort eligible galaxy IDs by ascending SHA-256 of UTF-8 string 'tg-sparc-v1|<Galaxy>'; first 31 are held out.

sample.primary_hypothesis_if_resumed: One shared positive K, estimated on training galaxies only; freeze all predictions and nuisances before scoring held-out rotation curves.

sfb_zip.content: on-sky 3.6-micron radial profiles; no inclination/extinction correction

source_model.stellar_surface_data_sufficiency: Radial surface photometry plus distances, inclination, a declared stellar M/L, and a fixed vertical profile can define an assumed 3D stellar density. SPARC's master-paper recipe is an exponential vertical disk with z_d=0.196 R_d^0.633 and spherical bulges.
stellar_nonuniqueness: radial profiles do not determine a unique 3D geometry or vertical structure
bar/lens/asymmetric structure and bulge flattening are simplified
outer extrapolations and photometric sky uncertainties matter
the published bulge-disk profiles are uncorrected and bulge light is linearly extrapolated at large radii
source_model.gas_surface_data_sufficiency: A deprojected HI surface-density profile/map, distance, orientation/warp treatment, gas outer taper, and an explicit gas vertical/flaring model could define an assumed 3D gas source; multiply HI by the declared helium factor (SPARC uses 1.33).
gas_inputs_missing: no HI surface-density profile/map is included in the staged SPARC basic downloads
Table 1 has total HI mass and an HI radius, not a radial density profile
Rotmod Vgas is a Newtonian component force curve, not a density map and not a unique substitute for one
gas thickness/flaring and molecular gas are not specified per galaxy
source_model.source_recovery: Acquire versioned HI surface-density profiles for the selected galaxies from the original SPARC source references; this is per-source recovery, not one complete small file on the official SPARC basic-data page. Do not substitute spherical inversion of Vgas.

boundary_contract.natural_isolated_choice: Regular at the center and phi -> 0 at infinity; for u=exp(-K phi), u -> 1. In a vacuum exterior, nabla^2 u=0.
boundary_contract.finite_domain_implementation_needed: Match the outer numerical solution to a decaying harmonic/multipole exterior and vary box radius and baryon taper until predicted velocities converge.
boundary_contract.paper_boundary_leakage: The supplied TG paper sets derivative boundaries at its first and last observed rotation-curve radii from observed velocities (Eqs. 41-42); the outer radius is defined as the furthest velocity point. This cannot be used for held-out galaxies.
boundary_contract.status: The physical isolated boundary can be declared without held-out data, but the current TG work has no 3D solver or validated exterior matching implementation; environmental/external-matter treatment is also unspecified.

blocking_inputs_and_work: Per-target HI surface-density profiles/maps and uncertainties, with enough outer-radius information to define a mass taper.
A frozen 3D geometry for stars, HI, helium, and any included molecular gas, with nuisance ranges and extrapolation rules fixed before held-out scoring.
A 3D elliptic TG solver implementing the isolated exterior match and box/taper convergence checks; never impose held-out Vobs as a boundary condition.
Fit universal K and any allowed training-only nuisance parameters on the 122-galaxy training set, then predict all radii of the 31 held-out galaxies without refitting.
download_policy: Only small official Table 1, stellar-decomposition ZIP, and bulge-luminosity table were fetched. No large survey products, HI cubes, or whole images were acquired.
regeneration_command: awk 'NF==19 && $18 ~ /^[12]$/ && $6+0>=30 {print $1}' work/data6/SPARC_Lelli2016c.mrt | while IFS= read -r galaxy; do digest=$(printf 'tg-sparc-v1|%s' "$galaxy" | sha256sum); printf '%s %s\n' "${digest%% *}" "$galaxy"; done | sort -k1,1 | awk 'NR<=31 {print $2}'
